project.projectDesc: Routes general questions to public knowledge sources and account-specific requests to authenticated customer-data paths.

caseStudy.summary: This customer-support system classifies incoming questions and routes them to either a general knowledge workflow or an account-specific data path. I contributed to a design that keeps general retrieval separate from authenticated access to private customer information.
caseStudy.challenge: A support assistant must answer common questions efficiently without treating private account data as ordinary public knowledge. The system needed to distinguish question types and apply the correct access path before generating a response.
caseStudy.architecture: The request first passes through authentication and query classification. General questions use a retrieval-augmented generation path over approved knowledge sources, while customer-specific questions are routed to the corresponding authorized data path.
caseStudy.diagram:
flowchart TD
  User[Customer] --> Auth[Authentication and permissions]
  Auth --> Classifier[Query classification]
  Classifier -->|General FAQ| RAG[Approved knowledge retrieval]
  Classifier -->|Account-specific| Account[Authorized customer data]
  RAG --> Answer[Response generation]
  Account --> Answer
  Answer --> User
contributions: Helped classify incoming requests as general FAQ or customer-account-specific questions.
Contributed routing between general retrieval and account-specific data paths.
Worked on authentication and secure permission workflows for private-data responses.
tradeoffs: Separate request paths make privacy boundaries clearer, at the cost of additional routing and authorization logic.
The system treats access control as part of request handling rather than relying on the language model to infer permissions.
Retrieval quality depends on curated knowledge sources, and the account-specific path must remain separate from general retrieval.

business: The workflow supports customer-service automation while separating general and account-specific requests.
quality: Authentication-aware routing distinguishes private account requests from general knowledge queries.
